title: Primary chunker output contract
description: The JSON the chunking model must return for ONE source document. Shape derived from the client's course-details demo template (segment -> subsegment -> chunk, with heading_path preserving hierarchy). The segment VOCABULARY is not the demo's page-section names: a source document is chunked so its chunks can route to per-segment extraction, so segment must be one of the project's 14 canonical retrieval segments, or 'unclassified'.
x-rules: Chunk at real structural boundaries: headings, sections, tables, lists, content blocks. Never fixed-size windows across unrelated content.
Each chunk belongs to exactly one segment and one subsegment.
Keep paragraphs, lists and tables together when they express one logical fact.
If a section has subsections, chunk at the subsection level; otherwise chunk the parent section.
Never invent a segment that the document does not actually cover. Use 'unclassified' instead -- an honest gap beats a forced label (Hard Constraint 4).
Never rewrite, normalise, summarise or correct source text. char_start/char_end must slice the exact original.
Ignore navigation, buttons, CSS, JavaScript, headers/footers and other UI-only content.

document_id.description: Echoed back from the request. Never invented.

segment.description: One of the 14 canonical retrieval segments, or 'unclassified'.

section_id.description: Source anchor where one exists -- an HTML id, or a PDF section label. Empty string when the document has none.

subsegment.description: Prefer the F-numbered field name this content supports (core_subjects, minimum_qualification, tuition_fee). Fall back to the document's own heading when no field fits. Never invent an F-field the content does not evidence.

field_ids.description: F-numbers this subsegment could support. Empty when none apply.

char_start.description: Inclusive offset into the parsed document text supplied in the request.

char_end.description: Exclusive offset. The pipeline slices the original text with these; the model must NOT return the text itself, so quoted evidence stays byte-identical to the source and citations remain verifiable (Hard Constraint 2).

heading_path.description: Ordered heading ancestry, outermost first, exactly as written in the document.

table_header.description: When a large table is split, the repeated column-header row, so each part stays interpretable alone.

course_scope.description: Whether this content is about one course, several, or the institution as a whole. A NIRF ranking table is institution_wide and must not be presented as a fact about one course.

chunks.table_header: Course Code | Course Title | L-T-P | Credits
